messages.subject: Two charts, same x-axis, but different geoms
parts:
Hi folks,

A couple of questions ...

I'd like to draw a time series chart on two stacked panels sharing the
same date axis. The top panel and larger panel as a line chart but
the lower panel(s) as area charts. These charts are reasonably common
in finance (eg http://www.quantmod.com/gallery/ ) - although this isnt
the exact purpose for me.

Secondly, I'd like to use the theme command to set the chart title to
be left justified and to have a sub-title (also left justified). Is
this possible?

Thanks in advance for any help

simeon

Hadley

I was afraid you might say that grid was the answer.  I still find it quite confusing to figure out.

I've got two issues.  Firstly, how to get rid of the axis titles, ticks and labels on the top graph (to give the same appearance as facet_wrap).  Secondly, how to line up the axes when the y-labels are longer on the bottom chart.

Here is some code to show what i mean.

require(ggplot2)
data(economics)
theme_set(theme_grey(20))

p <- ggplot(economics, aes(x=date,y=psavert))
p <-p+ geom_line()

pp <- ggplot(economics, aes(x=date,y=unemploy))
pp <-pp+ geom_area(fill=alpha("purple",
7/10),colour="black")

vplayout <- function(x, y)
viewport(layout.pos.row=x, layout.pos.col=y)
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(3,1)))
print(p, vp=vplayout(1:2,1))
print(pp, vp=vplayout(3,1))

any help or pointers very gratefully received.

simeon

> I'd like to draw a time series chart on two stacked panels sharing the

> the lower panel(s) as area charts.  These charts are reasonably common
> in finance (eg http://www.quantmod.com/gallery/ ) - although this isnt

The easiest way to go about this is to draw two separate plots on the
same device.  See the grid chapter for an example on how to do that.

> Secondly, I'd like to use the theme command to set the chart title to
> be left justified and to have a sub-title (also left justified).  Is
> this possible?

Unfortunately it's not currently possible to do either.  While you can
set the hjust in theme_text(), it doesn't work, because as well as
changing the alignment of the text, you also need to change the
position.  I'll think about how I could reparameterise theme_text() to
make that possible.

Similarly, there isn't currently any facility to add a subtitle.  It's
probably useful enough that I should add it - I'll put it on my to do
list.

Regards,

> Secondly, how to line up the axes when the y-labels are longer on the bottom

Hmmm, I had forgotten about those important issues. Maybe it's
possible to construct a data set that will work with faceting. Let's
see

library(ggplot2)
upper <- with(economics, data.frame(
date,
value = psavert,
position = "upper"
))

lower <- with(economics, data.frame(
date,
value = unemploy,
position = "lower"
))

ggplot(mapping = aes(date, value)) +
geom_line(data = upper) +
geom_area(data = lower) +
facet_wrap(~ position, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1)

Ok - that wasn't too hard (and I'm actually a little surprised that it
worked!). The careful construction of the dataset is the only
slightly tricky part - you need to add a new column that specifies the
position. You don't need to rename the value variables, but it does
save you a little typing in the plot construction.
